subject: Marker button & g.part4 error regarding sleeplog

messages.author: c9d28bd6f7b4d9e5
messages.subject: Marker button & g.part4 error regarding sleeplog
parts:
Hi,

first, thanks for the great work on the GGIR package! It's works quite easy for analysing .bin-files. I'm currently testing the script with only a few .bin-files.

My first question is regarding the marker button on the GeneActiv device. We asked participants to press the button when going to sleep and when getting out of bed in the morning.
Is or will there be a version of the GGIR package incoroporating this marker button?

Second, I'm struggling with part 4 of the g.shell.GGIR function, when using a sleeplog.
I'm getting the following error:

Error in match.names(clabs, names(xi)) : 
  names do not match previous names
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In which(sleeplog$id == as.numeric(accid)) : NAs introduced by coercion
2: In which(sleeplog$id == as.numeric(accid)) : NAs introduced by coercion

I'm not sure which names are meant in this error.
I do get some output, but only for one night.

I tried running the script without using a sleeplog, and then I also get the error regarding the names.


In the attachment is the used sleeplog, as wel as my script.

Thanks in advance!

Regards,
Chantal

messages.author: c9d28bd6f7b4d9e5
messages.subject: Re: Marker button & g.part4 error regarding sleeplog
parts:
In the sleep log, I now changed the id-names to 1.bin (etc) instead of just 1
This works to solve the problem I described above.

Since I would like to use the visualreport command, I addes this to the 4th part of the script.
I now get the following error:

Generate visual reports
[1] "File 21.bin"
Error in xy.coords(x, y, xlabel, ylabel, log) :
  'x' and 'y' lengths differ

Can anyone advise me how to solve this?

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Marker button & g.part4 error regarding sleeplog
parts:
Dear Chantal,
This looks like you have a different number of nights in your sleeplog then there are nights in your data? Please try changing the nnights argument. I have previously been contacted by your colleague (?) M.E. Verhoeff with similar questions. Did you talk to her?
I understand the need for additional functionality regarding the marker button. If you are interested I can develop this as a commercial consultancy.
Another option for you as scientist based in The Netherlands is to apply for funding via my employer www.esciencecenter.nl. These grants are aimed to enable scientific software innovation.
kind regards,
Vincent
